text: The Low Energy Gamma-Ray Imager (LEGRI) was a payload on the first mission of the Spanish MINISAT platform, operating from 1997 to 2002. Its primary goal was to demonstrate the feasibility of HgI2 detectors in space astronomy, offering imaging and spectroscopic capabilities within the 10-100 KeV energy range. LEGRI was launched successfully on April 21, 1997, using a Pegasus XL rocket and was activated on May 19, 1997. It remained active until February 2002. The instrument consisted of several components: the Detector Unit, Mask Unit, Power Supply, Digital Processing Unit, Star Sensor, and Ground Support Unit.
